findings.title: Adequate handwashing sinks properly supplied and accessible.
findings.comment: The handwashing sink where meats and cheeses are sliced lacked soap and paper towels. Discussed with the PIC and soap and paper towels were provided to the hand sink to correct the violation. Ensure that all hand sinks are equipped with hand soap, paper towels, and running warm water.
findings.citation_text: 6-301.11 Handwashing Cleanser, Availability. Each HANDWASHING SINK or group of 2 adjacent HANDWASHING SINKS shall be provided with a supply of hand cleaning liquid, powder, or bar soap.

findings.title: Food in good condition, safe, and unadulterated.
findings.comment: An unknown liquid food was observed actively producing bubbles, as the food was stored inside of the walk in cooler. The liquid food item appeared to be spoiled and not in safe condition to consume. The item also lacked date marking and an identification label. The liquid was pulled from the shelf to be discarded. Violation corrected. Ensure that Time/Temperature control (TCS) foods are date marked and are in good condition for consumption.
findings.citation_text: 3-101.11 Safe, Unadulterated, and Honestly Presented. FOOD shall be safe, unADULTERATED, and, as specified under § 3-601.12, honestly presented.

findings.title: Warewashing facilities: installed, maintained, and used; test strips.
findings.comment: Despite the service line being in operation, there wasn’t a sanitizer solution available. Discussed with PIC and a solution was created and tested at 300ppm (quat) to correct the violation. Ensure that sani solutions are always available if preparing, handling, or serving food.
findings.citation_text: 4-303.11(B) Cleaning Agents and Sanitizers, Availability. (B) Except for those that are generated on-site at the time of use, chemical SANITIZERS that are used to sanitize EQUIPMENT and UTENSILS as specified under Part 4-7, shall be provided and available for use during all hours of operation.

findings.title: Non-food contact surfaces clean.
findings.comment: The baffles of the hood suppression system above the fryers were a bit accumulated with dried grease. The PIC mentioned that the facility manual cleans the baffles, however, the system will need to be serviced by a professional to clean the internal work. Be sure to hire a professional hood service company to maintain duct work.
findings.citation_text: 4-601.11(C) Equipment, Food-Contact Surfaces, Nonfood-Contact Surfaces, and Utensils. (C) NonFOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT shall be kept free of an accumulation of dust, dirt, FOOD residue, and other debris.

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
findings.comment:
The following sinks are in need of repair:
- the current caulk on both triple sinks in the deli area are starting to pull from the wall 
- the current caulk on the triple sink in the meat/seafood area is starting to pull from the wall
Ensure that sinks are cleaned and recaulked to prevent debris accumulation and assure smooth and easily cleanable surfaces.
findings.citation_text: 6-501.11 Repairing. PHYSICAL FACILITIES shall be maintained in good repair.

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
findings.comment: Overall, the facility is in need of MAJOR CLEANING in the deli area. Floors, walls, ceilings, and sides of cooking equipment throughout the back of the house deli area contained heavy amounts of food debris and grease debris. The areas were shown to the PIC. Be sure that areas are cleaned and maintained clean as frequent as necessary.
findings.citation_text: 6-501.12 Cleaning, Frequency and Restrictions. (A) PHYSICAL FACILITIES shall be cleaned as often as necessary to keep them clean. (B) Except for cleaning that is necessary due to a spill or other accident, cleaning shall be done during periods when the least amount of FOOD is exposed such as after closing.

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
findings.comment: The sanitizer dispenser in the meat/seafood area appears to not be functioning properly. The sanitizer bucket, as well as the triple sink tested at 0ppm (quat). After changing the chemical’s bag, the solution remained at 0ppm (quat). The facility will utilize the butcher shop’s triple to sink to access sanitizer until the sink can be repaired. Ensure that the sanitizer solution tests at the manufacturer’s recommended concentration.
findings.citation_text: 4-601.11(A) Equipment, Food-Contact Surfaces, Nonfood-Contact Surfaces, and Utensils. (A) EQUIPMENT FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES and UTENSILS shall be clean to sight and touch.

findings.title: Contamination prevented during food preparation, storage and display.
findings.comment: There were at least 20 boxes observed on the floor of the shared walk in freezer. The boxes were pilled on top of each other and have started to fall onto the floor. An employee started to rearrange the freezer during the inspection to correct the violation. Ensure that food is stored in a manner that prevents contamination.
findings.citation_text: 3-305.11(A) Food Storage. (A) Except as specified in (B) and (C) of this section, FOOD shall be protected from contamination by storing the FOOD: (1) In a clean, dry location; (2) Where it is not exposed to splash, dust, or other contamination; and (3) At least 15 cm (6 inches) above the floor.

findings.citation_text: 5-205.15(B) System Maintained in Good Repair. A plumbing system shall be: (B) Maintained in good repair.

findings.citation_text: 4-501.114(A) Manual and Mechanical Warewashing Equipment, Chemical Sanitization - Temperature, pH, Concentration, and Hardness. A chemical SANITIZER used in a SANITIZING solution for a manual or mechanical operation at contact times specified under 4-703.11(C) shall meet the criteria specified under §7-204.11 Sanitizers, Criteria, shall be used in accordance with the EPA-registered label use instructions, and shall be used as follows: (A) A chlorine solution shall have a minimum temperature based on the concentration and PH of the solution as listed in the chart in 4-501.114 (A).

findings.title: Non-food contact surfaces clean.
findings.comment: The fan covers of the walk in chicken cooler were observed to have a significant buildup of dust. Discussed and shown to PIC. Ensure that cleaning of the fan covers occurs as often as necessary to prevent buildup and contamination of food items.

findings.title: Food separated and protected
findings.comment:
Observed a box of raw bacon stored above a box of jalapeño peppers in the meat department’s walk-in cooler. Discussed with PIC that raw meats should be stored beneath any ready-to-eat food item. The box of bacon was removed from the above shelf. Ensure that raw meats are always stored beneath RTE food items to prevent cross-contamination. 

3-302.11: (A) (1)-(2) FOOD shall be protected from cross contamination during storage, preparation, holding, and display (P). (3) FOOD shall be protected from cross contamination by cleaning visibly soiled containers, removing damaged containers, separating washed and unwashed produce (C).

findings.title: Proper date marking and disposition
findings.comment:
Observed several meat products to exceed the manufacturer’s use-by-date stored in the floor coolers. These items include but aren't limited to sliced deli meats, pork bacon, pork sausage, and ground sausage. The use-by-dates ranged from 4/28/2024 - 5/30/2024. Most of the meat items (bacon, pork sausage & deli meats) were manufactured, however, the other items (ground sausage) were processed on site. PIC mentioned that he has no knowledge of any written procedures on training employees to follow the “first in-first out” method and that employees are vocally trained to follow FIFO. The expired meat products were pulled from the coolers. The inspector suggested the PIC to have an employee thoroughly go through the cooler to check on use-by-dates. 

In the future, conduct a daily check on use-by-dates to ensure freshness of product. 


3-501.17: (A) Except for ROP, Refrigerated, RTE, TCS Food prepared and held in a food establishment for more than 24 hours shall be clearly marked to indicate the date/maximum of 7 days. Day of preparation is Day 1 (Pf). (B) Date marking may not exceed manufacturer’s use-by date (Pf). (C) Combined portions of food shall retain the date marking of the earliest-prepared food (Pf). (D) Approved date marking systems (C). (E)  Does not apply to repacked from a bulk container (C). (F) Does not apply to shellstock (C).  (G) Exemptions: prepared deli salads prepared according to 21 CFR 110; hard cheeses (39% moisture); semi-soft cheeses (50% or less); cultured dairy products (yogurt, sour cream, buttermilk); preserved fish (pickled herring, dried/salted); dry, fermented sausages (pepperoni); and salt-cured products (prosciutto and parma).

findings.title: Non-food contact surfaces clean
findings.comment:
Observed that vent covers of the walk in cooler (deli department) to be heavily soiled with debris. Discussed with PIC. PIC mentioned that an employee would clean the covers very soon. Ensure that the vent covers of the walk in cooler are cleaned frequently to prevent soil accumulation. 

4-601.11: (B) The FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of cooking EQUIPMENT and pans shall be kept free of encrusted grease deposits and other soil accumulations. (C) NonFOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT shall be kept free of an accumulation of dust, dirt, FOOD residue, and other debris.

findings.title: Plumbing installed; proper backflow devices
findings.comment:
Today’s follow-up was conducted to observe the hand washing sink in the back stock area of the produce department. The hand sink was observed in the same state as the original inspection that took place on 1/09/2024. The hand washing sink in the back stock area of the produce department did not have an adequate flow of hot water to wash hands properly. Discussed with produce manager and will followup to ensure that the hand-washing sink is properly working. An additional follow-up has been issued for 1/19/2024 to observe the mentioned hand sink.

5-205.15: A PLUMBING SYSTEM shall be: (A) Repaired according to LAW; P and (B) Maintained in good repair.

findings.title: Hands clean and properly washed
findings.comment:
An employee was observed using a bare hand to push the actuator for the paper towel dispenser after the hand washing process. Discussed with PIC and they’re instructed to educate employees on proper hand-washing procedures. Ensure that employees are using barriers to operate faucet handles and the actuator for paper towel dispensers.

2-301.12: (A) FOOD EMPLOYEES shall clean their hands and exposed portions of arms for at least 20 seconds. (B) FOOD EMPLOYEES shall use proper procedure (C) To prevent recontamination, FOOD EMPLOYEES may use barrier to operate faucet handles. (D) Automatic handwashing facility may be used if APPROVED.

findings.title: Food in good condition, safe, and unadulterated
findings.comment:
A dented can on the shelf was observed in the back stock area of the deli. Discussed the potentials of botulism with the manager and the dented can was discarded. Ensure that all canned items are free of dents and are in good condition to protect the content of the food. 

3-202.15: FOOD packages shall be in good condition and protect the integrity of the contents so that the FOOD is not exposed to ADULTERATION or potential contaminants.

findings.title: Food in good condition, safe, and unadulterated
findings.comment:
A tray of beets was observed to have mold on them in the produce area. Discussed with produce manager and the tray of moldy beets was discarded. Ensure that fresh produce is always safe and free of mold. 

3-101.11: FOOD shall be safe, unADULTERATED, and, honestly presented.

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized
findings.comment:
The ice machine in the produce backstock area contained mold at the top inside of the machine. Discussed cleaning the machine with produce manager. The machine is used by many departments (deli, meat/butcher, produce etc). Ensure that all food contact surfaces are cleaned regularly. The ice machine was cleaned and corrected during the inspection. 

4-601.11: (A) EQUIPMENT FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES and UTENSILS shall be clean to sight and touch.

findings.title: Proper cold holding temperatures
findings.comment:
Pizza breads, cut bagged lettuces, and salad dressings were observed at temperatures between 45F - 55F. The location of the two coolers was to the left of the main produce entrance area and the deli’s open pizza bread cooler. Discussed with both the produce manager and deli manager and foods that were out of temp were discarded. Ensure that TCS foods are at 41F or less at all time.  

3-501.16: (A) (2) TCS FOOD shall be maintained at 41F or less. (B) EGGS not treated to destroy Salmonellae shall be stored at 45F or less.

findings.title: Toxic substances properly identified, stored, and used
findings.comment:
A bottle of tile cleaner to remove mold was stored above the triple sink in the shared back-stock area of the meat/deli/bakery. Discussed with meat manager and the bottle was moved to correct the violation. Ensure that all non-food grade chemicals are stored away from food-contact surfaces. 

7-201.11: (A)-(B) POISONOUS MATERIALS shall be stored to prevent contamination of FOOD and FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES by separating or locating MATERIALS in area away or below FOOD and FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES (use partition or store below).

findings.title: Proper cooling methods used; adequate equipment for temperature control
findings.comment:
The coolers from line item 22 are not functioning correctly and are in need of repair/adjustment. Discussed with the produce manager and the deli manager. A followup will occur in 2 weeks. Ensure that cold holding equipment is always functioning properly. 

4-301.11: EQUIPMENT for cooling and heating FOOD, and holding cold and hot FOOD, shall be sufficient in number and capacity to provide FOOD temperatures.

findings.title: Plumbing installed; proper backflow devices
findings.comment:
The hand washing sink in the back stock area of the produce area did not have an adequate flow of hot water to wash hands properly. Discussed with produce manager and will followup to ensure that the hand-washing sink is properly working. 

5-205.15: A PLUMBING SYSTEM shall be: (A) Repaired according to LAW; P and (B) Maintained in good repair.

findings.title: Adequate ventilation and lighting; designated areas used
findings.comment:
The shielding on the light bulb in the butcher freezer was observed to be cracked. Discussed with meat manager. Ensure that light bulb shields are maintained and are in good condition. 

6-202.11: Light bulbs shall be shielded, coated or otherwise shatter-resistant in certain areas.

findings.title: Adequate handwashing sinks properly supplied and accessible
findings.citation_text:
5-205.11 Handwashing sink at front service area of deli was used to rinse a knife prior to cleaning and sanitizing. Proper use of handwashing sink was discussed. Ensure handwashing sinks are used only for handwashing. The 3 part sink should be used for all other tasks. 
Handwashing sinks are to be accessible at all times and used only for handwashing.

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized
findings.citation_text:
4-501.114 Quat solutions in sani-buckets at front service area of deli and in cooking area were observed at 100ppm. Fresh solutions at 200ppm were provided. Provide fresh solution as needed throughout daily operations. Ensure use of quat test strips to verify sanitizer is at proper concentration when dispensed for use. 
A quaternary ammonia compound solution shall be used in accordance with the EPA-registered label use instructions and be maintained at the concentration as indicated by the manufacturer's use directions included in the labeling. Ensure product is maintained at 150-400ppm as required per product label directions.

findings.title: Proper hot holding temperatures
findings.citation_text:
3-501.16 (A)(1) Baked chicken in hot case was observed with surface temperatures of 121F-140F and internal temperatures of 126F-142F. Deli manager noted baked chicken is one of the first items prepared for hot service but had not been in the hot case for more than an hour. Baked chicken was reheated prior to placing back in hot case for lunch service.
Except during preparation, cooking, or cooling, or when time is used as the public health control, cooked hot foods that require time/temperature control for safety shall be maintained at 135F/above.

findings.title: Washing fruits and vegetables
findings.citation_text:
3-302.15 1) Produce wash concentration was less than 30ppm and near 0ppm when initially checked, and the product (Produce Maxx) requires a concentration of 30-60ppm. Produce prep employee stated the solution being used to soak berries prior to cutting was dispensed ~30 minutes prior. Solution was discarded, and fresh solution provided at 60ppm. Employee was advised to monitor the concentration of produce wash and ensure solution is refreshed as needed during prep so concentration is maintained at 30-60ppm as required.
2) While discussing practices, employee in produce prep area indicated freshly cut cantaloupe was not washed prior to cutting and portioning in containers with cut melon for retail case. Based on information provided, employee was asked to discard all portions containing cut cantaloupe because melons were said to be washed prior to cutting. Employee discarded all portions of cut melon and cantaloupe, including containers that only had melon. Whole cantaloupe intended for use was placed in produce wash for cleaning. **See general comments for additional information**
Except as specified in (B) of this section and except for whole, raw fruits and vegetables that are intended for washing by the consumer before consumption, raw fruits and vegetables shall be thoroughly washed in water to remove soil and other contaminants before being cut, combined with other ingredients, cooked, served, or offered for human consumption in ready to eat form.
Fruits and vegetables may be washed by using chemicals as specified under § 7-204.12.
Devices used for on-site generation of chemicals meeting the requirements specified in 21 CFR 173.315, Chemicals used in the washing or to assist in the peeling of fruits and vegetables, for the washing of raw, whole fruits and vegetables shall be used in accordance with the manufacturer’s instructions.

findings.title: Non-food contact surfaces clean
findings.citation_text:
4-602.13 Carts, shelves, and racks throughout deli department were in need of detail cleaning. Food splash, general buildup, and seasonings were observed on general surfaces of carts, shelves, and racks throughout the deli department including in the chicken cooler, by front handwashing sink, and throughout back cooking/frying area. Ensure cleaning as needed for non-food contact surfaces.
Nonfood contact surfaces shall be cleaned at a frequency necessary to eliminate buildup of grease, food splash and general debris.

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and clean
findings.citation_text:
6-501.12 DELI 1)  Floor throughout the back cooking and prep area was soiled with general buildup of grease and food debris under equipment and behind cooking equipment. 
2) Ponding dirty water was observed at clean-outs in the back prep and dish washing area.
3) Wall and attached plumbing under warewashing sink were soiled with splash/general buildup. 
4) Walls behind cooking equipment were soiled with general buildup and grease.
BUTCHER SHOP 1) Floor along wall by handwashing sink and under 3 part sink was was soiled with buildup of food crumbs and general debris. 
Ensure cleaning of floors, walls, and attached equipment as needed.
Physical facilities shall be cleaned as often as necessary to keep them clean.

findings.title: Proper eating, tasting, drinking, or tobacco use
findings.citation_text:
2-401.11 Employee working at chicken fry station was observed chewing gum while breading chicken. Employee discarded gum at request of inspector. Ensure staff are not eating while working in food prep/service area
Employees shall eat, including gum/candy, only in designated areas where the contamination of exposed food; clean equipment, utensils, and linens; unwrapped single service and single use articles; or other items needing protection cannot result.

findings.title: Hands clean and properly washed
findings.citation_text:
2-301.14 Deli employee left the area and returned to wait on a customer. Gloves were put on with first washing hands. Proper handwahsing was discussed. Employee washed hands prior to putting on new gloves. Ensure proper handwashing occurs upon entering the work area, prior to putting on gloves and between glove changes. 
Food Employees shall clean their hands and exposed portions of their arms immediately before engaging in food preparation including working with exposed food, clean equipment and utensils, and unwrapped single-service and single-use articles. Hands shall also be washed after engaging in other activities that contaminate the hands and prior to donning gloves.

findings.title: Food separated and protected
findings.citation_text:
3-302.11 Tray of raw chicken was observed above a tray with thawing fish on a storage rack in the Deli chicken cooler. Tray of chicken was moved below fish to allow for proper storage.
Food shall be protected from cross contamination be separating raw animal foods from each other such as beef, fish, lamb, pork, and poultry during storage, preparation, holding, and display arranging each type of food in equipment so that cross contamination of one type with another is prevented.

findings.title: Food separated and protected
findings.citation_text:
3-304.15 Employee working in produce prep area left with gloves hands to retrieve additional containers of berries from a retail case. Upon returning to the prep area gloves were not changed. Proper glove use was discussed. Gloves were changed prior to continuing with prep. Ensure glove changes between tasks and upon exiting and re-entering prep areas of all departments. 
Best practice is to remove gloves when stepping away from tasks and exiting area as a handwash will be required in addition to a glove change. 
Single use gloves shall be used for only one task, used for no other purpose, and discarded when damaged or soiled, or when interruptions occur in the operation.

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized
findings.citation_text:
4-501.114 Quat solutions in sani-buckets at deli service counter and in Butcher Shop were observed at 100ppm. Fresh solutions at 200ppm were provided. Ensure solutions are changed as needed and maintained at proper concentration of 150-400ppm.
A quaternary ammonia compound solution shall be used in accordance with the EPA-registered label use instructions and be maintained at the concentration as indicated by the manufacturer's use directions included in the labeling. Use test strips to verify concentration and make sure water temperature is set according to product directions. Also, consider pre-soaking wiping cloths with sanitizer prior to storage in a fresh solution to help minimize absorption of chemical out of solution into wiping cloths.

findings.title: Proper cold holding temperatures
findings.citation_text:
3-501.16 1. Bags of beef and noodles and chicken and noodles were observed with surface temperatures at 66F-67F. Products were said to be heated in the steamer prior to storage in the walk-in cooler earlier in the day. Employee stated products were going to be used soon, but they were unsure how long products were at room temperature. Products were placed in walk-in cooler to chill items prior to use. Ensure cold TCS foods are only removed from coolers as needed for prep and placed back in coolers as quickly as possible to avoid prolonged temperature abuse. If interruption in prep occurs, places foods back in coolers to cold hold until proper attention can be provided for prep.

2. Portions of lasagna and other prepared meal items were observed with surface temperatures above 60F in the prep area. Products were placed in the retail display cooler without first chilling. Upon request of assistant manager, the products in question were moved to the walk-in cooler to chill prior to placing back in the display case. Ensure products are properly chilled and at an internal temperature of 41F/below prior to storage in retail display coolers.
Except during preparation, cooking, or cooling, or when time is used as a public health control, cold TCS foods shall be maintained at 41F/below.

findings.title: Toxic substances properly identified, stored, and used
findings.citation_text:
7-102.11 Chemical in spray bottle labeled as sanitizer at the Butcher Shop was observed to be orange in color and a tested at 400ppm+. Other spray bottles of sanitizer contained chemical that was clear in color and tested at 200ppm. Butcher Shop employee noted the bottle was filled at the dispenser by the mop sink. Sanitizer is not available at said dispenser, which is connected to window cleaner, disinfectants, and a chlorinated cleaner. Product was removed from Butcher Shop by assistant manager for discard. Staff will be re-educated on proper chemical use and obtaining sanitizer from chemical dispensers in their departments.
Working containers used for storing poisonous or toxic materials such as cleaners and sanitizers taken from bulk supplies shall be clearly and individually identified with the common name of the material

findings.title: Food and non-food contact surfaces cleanable, properly designed, constructed, and used
findings.citation_text:
4-202.16 Gaskets around door to deli walk-in cooler were torn and missing in large sections. Replace the gaskets on the deli walk-in cooler door and other coolers and freezers as needed.
Nonfood contact surfaces shall be free of unnecessary ledges, projections, and crevices, and designed and constructed to allow easy cleaning and to facilitate maintenance.

findings.title: Non-food contact surfaces clean
findings.citation_text:
4-602.13 The following non-food contact surfaces were soiled: 
1. PRODUCE DEPT: Storage shelving below prep counter (general buildup/debris);
2. DELI DEPT: a) storage containers for labels at front service counter (grimy buildup) and  b) chicken cooler shelving (general buildup);  and
3. BUTCHER SHOP: floor fan (heavy dust accumulation).

findings.title: Hot and cold water available; adequate pressure
findings.citation_text:

Lack of cold water appeared to be related to a connection with the mister at the produce case. Hot and cold water was available at all fixtures in the produce prep area after repair occurred. 
Hot and cold water under pressure shall be provided to all fixtures, equipment, and nonfood equipment that are required to use water.

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and clean
findings.citation_text:
6-501.12 1. The condensing unit in the deli chicken cooler was observed with dust accumulation on fan covers and wiring underneath. Ceiling above was also soiled with dust.
2. Floors under and around handwashing sinks were soiled with general buildup, especially in the Butcher Shop and front service area of deli.
3. Floor was soiled with grease and food debris under and around fryers and other equipment in back deli prep area.
Ensure cleaning of physical facilities as needed and maintain them clean.
Physical facilities shall be cleaned as often as necessary to keep them clean.

findings.title: Warewashing facilities: installed, maintained, & used; test strips
findings.comment:
Observed no sani buckets in use in the deli during the inspection. An employee stated the buckets had just been dumped to get changed. Ensure sani buckets are remade after they are discarded. Sani bucket was made during the inspection. 
4-303.11: (A) Cleaning agents used to clean EQUIPMENT shall be provided and available during all hours of operation. (B) Chemical SANITIZERS shall be provided and available during all hours of operation.

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and clean
findings.comment:
6-501.12: Observed the floor behind the ovens in the deli cook line to be heavily soiled with grease and food debris near the wall. Ensure this surface is cleaned regularly so it maintains clean. 
(A) PHYSICAL FACILITIES shall be cleaned as often as necessary to keep them clean. (B) Except for cleaning that is necessary due to a spill or other accident, cleaning shall be done during periods when the least amount of FOOD is exposed such as after closing.

findings.title: Adequate handwashing sinks properly supplied and accessible
findings.comment:
Observed a spoon with sauce sitting in the hand sink at the start of the inspection. The spoon was moved to correct the violation. Ensure hand sinks are used for hand washing only. 
5-205.11: (A) A HANDWASHING SINK shall be maintained so that it is accessible at all times for EMPLOYEE use. (B) A HANDWASHING SINK may not be used for purposes other than handwashing. (C) An automatic handwashing facility shall be used in accordance with manufacturer’s instructions.

findings.title: Toxic substances properly identified, stored, and used
findings.comment:
7-201.11: Observed sanitizer buckets to be stored on top of the prep table where food is prepared. These should be placed below the level where food is prepared to avoid contamination of food with sanitizer. Sani buckets were moved during the inspection. 
(A)-(B) POISONOUS MATERIALS shall be stored to prevent contamination of FOOD and FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES by separating or locating MATERIALS in area away or below FOOD and FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES (use partition or store below).

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and clean
findings.comment:
6-501.12: Observed the floor underneath the 3 part sink and ovens in the deli cook line to be heavily soiled with grease and food debris near the wall. Ensure this surface is cleaned regularly so it maintains clean. 
(A) PHYSICAL FACILITIES shall be cleaned as often as necessary to keep them clean. (B) Except for cleaning that is necessary due to a spill or other accident, cleaning shall be done during periods when the least amount of FOOD is exposed such as after closing.

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized
findings.comment:
4-602.11: Observed a cook that took the temperature of the cooked chicken and then wiped the food thermometer on his apron and then stuck it in his apron slot to hold it. Ensure that proper cleaning techniques are used when utilizing equipment to reduce the risks of contamination.
4-602.11: (A) FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES shall be cleaned before each use, each time there is a change in work, between uses of raw FOODS to RTE FOODS, before using FOOD TEMPERATURE MEASURING DEVICE, and when contamination has occurred.

findings.title: Adequate handwashing sinks properly supplied and accessible
findings.citation_text: 5-205.11 (A) Observed an old sani bucket to be sitting in the hand sink. Hand sinks can only be used for hand washing. The sani bucket was moved during the inspection.

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized
findings.citation_text: 4-601.11(A)  (Pf) Observed the can opener to be soiled with food debris. The can opener was moved to the dish area during the inspection. Wash, rinse, sanitize food-contact surfaces routinely. Reference 4-601.11(A).

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and clean
findings.citation_text: 6-501.16  (C) Mop was found stored incorrectly in-between use. The mop was stored inside the mop bucket. Mops shall be placed in a position that allows them to air-dry without soiling walls, equipment, or supplies. The mop was moved to a position that allowed it to drip dry.  Reference 6-501.16.

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized
findings.citation_text: 4-501.114  (P) Quat sanitizer concentrations in sani buckets were measured at 50 ppm. Employee changed the sani buckets during the inspection. Sani buckets must have a concentration of 200 to 400 ppm of quat.

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and clean
findings.citation_text: 6-201.11  (C) Observed floor tiles broken in the prep are and near the 3 compartment sink and holes above the 3 compartment sink during the inspection. Ensure that tiles are repaired or replaced and holes are sealed to ensure they are smooth and easily cleanable. Additionally, base coving near the door leading to the deli was starting to come apart from the wall. Ensure coving is resealed to the wall or replaced to prevent water from entering the gap.

findings.title: Allergen training as required
findings.comment: 410 ILCS 625 Sec. 3.07 Online food allergen awareness training has not been completed by management. PIC stated that allergen training is available in the company portal.

findings.title: Hands clean and properly washed
findings.citation_text:
2-301.14 Employee was observed putting on gloves without first washing hands prior to handling deli meat. Prior to putting on gloves the employee was observed using a sanitizer solution and wiping down surfaces. Handwashing was discussed. Employee washed hands prior to continuing with next task.
Food Employees shall clean their hands and exposed portions of their arms immediately before engaging in food preparation including working with exposed food, clean equipment and utensils, and unwrapped single-service and single-use articles. Hands must also be washed after engaging in any activities that contaminate the hands, between tasks, and prior to putting on gloves.

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized
findings.citation_text:
4-602.11 Can opener was observed to be soiled with general buildup. Can opener was taken to dish are for ware washing. Clean and sanitize the can opener between uses and up to every 4 hours after continuous use.

While speaking with manager about cleaning frequency for slicers it was discovered the slicers are not getting washed, rinse, and sanitized up to every 4hrs after continuous use. Manager noted slicers are disassembled nightly but was unsure as to cleaning process. Slicers are wiped down with sanitizer throughout operations daily. 
Deli manager stated the frequency/process for deli slicers can be changed if necessary. Management was advised to have the deli staff change the procedure and make sure all slicer components used for deli meats and cheeses are properly cleaned and sanitized up to every 4hrs after continuous use.
Equipment food contact surfaces and utensils used with time/temperature control for safety food shall be cleaned and sanitized throughout the day at least every 4 hours.

findings.title: Proper hot holding temperatures
findings.citation_text:
3-501.16 Roasted chicken at the left end of the hot case was observed with surface temperatures at 109F-115F and internal temperatures at 119F-125F. The door on the left end of the hot case was observed open and tongs extended out of the case when inspector first walked up to the area. Other foods in the case were observed with surface and internal temperatures at 135F/above. It would appear the door being left open caused the temperature to drop. The chicken finished cooked at 150pm with an internal temperature of 179F based on the temperature log. Chicken was reheated to 165F prior to being placed back in the case for hot holding.  
 Except during preparation, cooking, or cooling, or when time is used as the public health control, cooked hot foods that require time/temperature control for safety shall be maintained at 135°F/above. PRIORITY

findings.title: Proper cold holding temperatures
findings.citation_text:
3-501.16 Upon arrival two tubs of shredded chicken were observed out on in the front service area. Chicken was unattended and not currently being prepared, but staff were working with the chicken prior to inspector's arrival to make chicken salad. Surface temperatures were at 59F/60F, and the internal temperature of chicken in one tub was observed at 55F-56F. Chicken was placed back in the walkin cooler until staff had time to finish prep.
Mostaccoli in the walkin cooler had surface and internal temperatures at 45F and 51F respectively. Person who prepared product was not present, but manager spoke with employee via phone. Based on information provided the product was prepared using frozen, thawed/chilled noodles and a pre-chilled meat sauce and should have been at proper temperature. The product was prepared within the last hour and placed in the freezer to help quickly drop the temperature. Management discussed moving the location of the cooling rack, which is currently right by the door to the walkin.
Except during preparation, cooking, or cooling, or when time is used as a public health control, cold TCS foods shall be maintained at 41°F/below

findings.title: Thermometers provided & accurate
findings.citation_text:
4-203.11 Food thermometers were questioned as to accuracy when staff and inspector were in the process of verifying the internal temperature of a product in the walkin cooler. All thermometers were checked with ice water slurry. Inspector's digital stem thermometer read at 32.5F, while the two metal stem thermometers used by the facility were observed reading between 26F-28F. Management calibrated thermometers to 32°F in an ice water solution. Calibration frequency was discussed.
Food temperature measuring devices that are scaled only in Fahrenheit shall be accurate to ±2°F in the intended range of use.

findings.title: Wiping cloths: properly used and stored
findings.citation_text:
3-304.14 Damp wiping cloth was observed on a prep table next to sani-bucket in the back prep area. Wiping cloth in question was placed in solution by manager. Proper storage of wiping cloths between uses was discussed.
Cloths in-use for wiping counters and other equipment surfaces shall be held between uses in a chemical sanitizer solution maintained at proper concentration for the sanitizer product being used.

findings.title: Utensils, equipment & linens: properly stored, dried, & handled
findings.citation_text:
4-903.11 Several clean knives were observed stored in the crevice between the removable knife rack and the wall in the back prep area. The top of the knife rack was also soiled with general buildup. Knife rack and knives in question were removed and taken to dish area for ware washing. Proper storage of clean utensils was discussed. The crevices between walls and equipment are not considered clean surfaces. 
Clean utensils and equipment shall be stored in a clean, dry location, where they are not exposed to splash, dust, or other contamination. Clean the removable knife storage rack daily/as needed.

findings.title: Hands clean and properly washed
findings.comment: Observed an employee handle a cell phone and credit card, and then put on gloves and begin working without washing her hands.
findings.citation_text: 2-301.14  (P) Food employee entered kitchen and handled food without washing hands. Food employee must practice good hygiene by properly washing hands when changing tasks. Reference 2-301.14.

findings.title: Non-food contact surfaces clean
findings.citation_text: 4-602.13  (C) Soil and food residue present on several non food contact surfaces throughout the kitchen. Clean all non-food contact surfaces frequently to prevent soil accumulation.  Reference 4-602.13.

findings.title: Allergen training as required
findings.comment: PA-100-0367 - All certified food managers working in a restaurant must complete additional allergen training using an approved allergen awareness training program.
